subject: community-medicine
title: Malaria Case Finding: Indices and Artemisinin Combination Therapy

steps.title: Slide positivity rate in outbreak detection
steps.tx: In community fever surveillance, the **slide positivity rate** quantifies the proportion of examined blood smears demonstrating Plasmodium trophozoites or gametocytes, expressed as positive slides divided by total slides examined times one hundred. A sudden doubling of this metric above seasonal baselines alerts epidemiologists to localized focal transmission, prompting immediate indoor residual spraying, mass blood surveys and antimalarial replenishment.
steps.say: A sudden jump in slide positivity rate above historical seasonal levels exposes an emerging outbreak. Epidemiologists respond with contact tracing, indoor spraying and extra drug supplies.

steps.tx: Under oil immersion the technician searches a Giemsa stained thick film for malaria parasites. In community fever surveillance the **slide positivity rate** is the percentage of examined smears that show Plasmodium trophozoites or gametocytes. It is positive slides divided by all slides examined, then multiplied by one hundred. A sudden doubling above the seasonal baseline signals focal transmission and calls for indoor residual spraying, mass blood surveys, and fresh antimalarial stocks.
steps.say: Thick films read under oil show whether fever surveys are finding malaria parasites. Slide positivity is positive smears divided by all smears, times one hundred. A sudden rise to twice the usual seasonal level means local spread and should trigger spraying, wider blood surveys, and more drug stocks.

steps.title: Annual blood examination rate as a validity filter
steps.tx: Public health officers validate low case incidence by auditing the **annual blood examination rate**, which reflects surveillance intensity across the sub-centre population over twelve months. If an administrative block reports zero cases but exhibits an examination rate below five percent, transmission is concealed by negligent case finding; true low endemicity can only be claimed when the annual rate exceeds ten percent.
steps.say: Low case numbers mean nothing if the annual blood examination rate stays below ten percent. Weak screening conceals transmission, while robust screening proves true interruption.

left.title: Inadequate screening (ABER < 10%)
points: Apparent zero cases is an artifact

right.title: Adequate screening (ABER >= 10%)
points: Low case counts reflect true suppression

steps.title: Peripheral blood smear examination standards
steps.tx: Microscopic diagnosis depends on the gold-standard **thick and thin smear** prepared on a single glass slide from finger-prick capillary blood. The thick smear dehaemoglobinises red cells to concentrate parasites twenty to thirty-fold for rapid detection, whereas the methanol-fixed thin smear preserves red blood cell architecture, enabling differential identification between the delicate rings of Plasmodium falciparum and enlarged, amoeboid vivax trophozoites.
steps.say: A thick smear dehaemoglobinises red cells to concentrate parasites for detection. A thin smear fixes cell shape, allowing pathologists to distinguish falciparum from vivax.

vis.alt: Microscopic smear showing ring forms of Plasmodium falciparum and amoeboid forms of Plasmodium vivax
vis.caption: Ring forms and gametocytes of Plasmodium falciparum alongside amoeboid trophozoites of Plasmodium vivax. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.title: First-line chemotherapy: artemisinin combination therapy
steps.tx: National malaria guidelines mandate **artemisinin-based combination therapy** for all confirmed cases of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria to ensure rapid biomass reduction and forestall resistance emergence. Artemisinin derivatives rapidly destroy intraerythrocytic asexual stages within two hours, while their slower-clearing partner drugs eliminate remaining residual parasites over subsequent weeks, preventing recrudescence and curing the host completely.
steps.say: Artemisinin combinations destroy billions of parasites within hours, while their slower partner drugs clear residual parasites over several weeks, preventing recrudescence.

right.title: Partner drug component
points: Maintains inhibitory blood levels for weeks

steps.title: Regional ACT policies across India
steps.tx: The national program stratifies **artemisinin partner regimens** by geographic resistance patterns across the country. In northeastern states where antifolate resistance mutations are widespread, artemether-lumefantrine given over three days serves as the exclusive first-line combination, whereas in the remainder of India, co-formulated oral artesunate combined with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine remains the designated first-line therapy for uncomplicated falciparum infections.
steps.say: Artemether-lumefantrine is the first-line choice in northeastern states due to antifolate resistance. Artesunate with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine is used across the rest of the country.

rows: High prevalence of dhfr and dhps mutations
Efficacy preserved across central and southern belts

steps.title: Artesunate combination dosing and administration
steps.tx: For non-pregnant adults outside the northeast, **artesunate dosing** delivers four milligrams per kilogram body weight once daily for three consecutive days, combined with a single therapeutic dose of sulfadoxine twenty-five milligrams per kilogram and pyrimethamine one point two five milligrams per kilogram on day one. To destroy infectious sexual stages, a single dose of primaquine is added on day two.
steps.say: Patients take artesunate daily for three days, with a single dose of sulfadoxine and pyrimethamine on day one. A single primaquine dose follows on day two to kill gametocytes.

steps.title: Severe malaria management with intravenous artesunate
steps.tx: When danger signs or vital organ dysfunction appear, clinical protocols require emergency **intravenous artesunate** at two point four milligrams per kilogram administered immediately at zero, twelve and twenty-four hours, continuing once daily until the patient tolerates oral fluids. Intravenous artesunate demonstrates superior survival over intravenous quinine in randomised clinical trials, eliminating cardiac arrhythmia risks and hypoglycaemic complications.
steps.say: Intravenous artesunate is given immediately at zero, twelve and twenty-four hours for severe malaria. It improves survival over quinine and avoids life-threatening arrhythmias.

nodes.label: Switch to full oral ACT when alert

steps.title: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance monitoring
steps.tx: National research institutes conduct longitudinal **antimalarial therapeutic efficacy monitoring** across sentinel surveillance districts to detect emerging drug insensitivity. Point mutations in the dihydropteroate synthase and dihydrofolate reductase genes confer resistance to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, while kelch-13 propeller gene mutations herald artemisinin tolerance; whenever treatment failure rates exceed ten percent, the national technical committee updates the designated first-line drug.
steps.say: Sentinel laboratories monitor parasite genes for mutations in dhfr, dhps and kelch-13. If treatment failure in an area exceeds ten percent, the national drug policy changes.

steps.title: Treatment monitoring and parasite clearance
steps.tx: Clinical response evaluation requires structured **parasitological cure assessment** on days three, seven, fourteen and twenty-eight following therapy initiation. Early treatment failure is diagnosed if danger signs emerge or parasitaemia persists on day three, whereas late treatment failure represents parasite recurrence between days seven and twenty-eight, distinguishing true treatment refractoriness from reinfection through molecular genotyping of parasite polymorphic loci.
steps.say: Follow patients with blood smears on days three, seven, fourteen and twenty-eight. Parasites remaining on day three signal treatment failure, demanding second-line therapy.
